evidence.claim: Marcos appointed retired UP professor Clarita Carlos as National Security Adviser under his administration.
evidence.title: Marcos names nat’l security adviser, DAR chief
evidence.excerpt: Marcos appointed retired UP professor Clarita Carlos as National Security Adviser under his administration.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: State newswire reporting an announced Cabinet appointment with photo and caption context.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 ruler-period evidence, before and immediately after inauguration.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Marcos's staffing choice.
contrary_evidence: Appointment alone does not prove restraint or effectiveness.
Carlos later voiced policy intent, but implementation still needed corroboration.

evidence.claim: Incoming national security adviser Clarita Carlos said she wanted to stop red-tagging and described it as not productive, while HRW noted the practice had been carried out through the Duterte-era task force.
evidence.title: New Philippine Security Adviser Urges End to 'Red-Tagging'
evidence.excerpt: Incoming national security adviser Clarita Carlos said she wanted to stop red-tagging and described it as not productive, while HRW noted the practice had been carried out through the Duterte-era task force.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent human-rights reporting with direct quote and institutional context.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 ruler-period evidence at the start of Marcos's term.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but materially relevant because Carlos was Marcos's incoming security adviser and part of his chosen team.
contrary_evidence: This is a stated intention, not proof that red-tagging stopped.
The same report says the task force had been responsible for much of the practice.

evidence.claim: CHR welcomed Justice Secretary Menardo Guevarra's call to end red-tagging and warned that labeling groups without sufficient evidence can expose them to attacks and chills free expression.
evidence.title: Statement of Executive Director, Atty. Jacqueline Ann de Guia, welcoming the statement of the Justice Secretary calling an end to red-tagging and respect for freedoms
evidence.publisher: Commission on Human Rights of the Philippines
evidence.excerpt: CHR welcomed Justice Secretary Menardo Guevarra's call to end red-tagging and warned that labeling groups without sufficient evidence can expose them to attacks and chills free expression.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official national human-rights institution statement directly describing the risk of red-tagging.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 ruler-period evidence during Marcos's transition.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect; it reflects institutions around Marcos's incoming administration, not a direct order from Marcos.
contrary_evidence: A statement by CHR does not prove the executive branch adopted the advice.
The persistence of red-tagging later in 2022 limits any positive inference.

evidence.claim: The Commission on Human Rights reminded police to exercise maximum tolerance during peaceful protests and warned against water cannons or firearms while monitoring SONA rallies for abuses.
evidence.title: Bongbong Marcos' first SONA: It's all about economy
evidence.excerpt: The Commission on Human Rights reminded police to exercise maximum tolerance during peaceful protests and warned against water cannons or firearms while monitoring SONA rallies for abuses.
evidence.source_locator: paragraphs on CHR reminder and monitoring
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent local reporting quoting CHR guidance issued for Marcos's first SONA.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect; it concerns the policing environment under Marcos rather than a personal order from him.
contrary_evidence: The need for this warning indicates protest sensitivity and a nontrivial repression risk.
The article itself does not show whether the guidance fully worked.

evidence.claim: Police officers blocked Filipino activists from marching during a protest marking Marcos's first 100 days in office.
evidence.title: Protest during Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr's first 100 days in office
evidence.excerpt: Police officers blocked Filipino activists from marching during a protest marking Marcos's first 100 days in office.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters photo caption directly documents police obstruction of a protest in Marcos's first 100 days.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirectly attributable to the policing environment under Marcos's administration.
contrary_evidence: A photo caption captures one event, not the whole protest climate.
It does not show Marcos personally ordered the blockage.

evidence.claim: Amnesty said the Marcos administration's decision not to rejoin the ICC would not stop the investigation into Duterte-era crimes because there was no evidence of genuine domestic investigations and prosecutions.
evidence.title: Philippines: Decision to not rejoin the ICC statute will not prevent investigation
evidence.excerpt: Amnesty said the Marcos administration's decision not to rejoin the ICC would not stop the investigation into Duterte-era crimes because there was no evidence of genuine domestic investigations and prosecutions.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Clear advocacy statement anchored in the administration's announced decision and Amnesty's accountability assessment.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly about a Marcos administration accountability choice.
contrary_evidence: The administration argued domestic investigations were sufficient.
This concerns inherited abuses, but Marcos still chose the non-rejoin position.

evidence.claim: The Dahas Project data showed 152 drug-related killings in the first five months of the Marcos administration, exceeding the 149 killings recorded in the final six months of the Duterte government.
evidence.title: Drug killings under Marcos Jr. surpass those killed in last six months of Duterte
evidence.publisher: VERA Files / UP Third World Studies Center (Dahas Project)
evidence.excerpt: The Dahas Project data showed 152 drug-related killings in the first five months of the Marcos administration, exceeding the 149 killings recorded in the final six months of the Duterte government.
evidence.source_locator: opening paragraph and first data summary
evidence.source_confidence_reason: University-based monitoring data reported in an investigative outlet, with clear comparative counts.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly relevant to Marcos's first five months in office.
contrary_evidence: The report says Marcos adopted a different strategy, but the killings continued at a high level.
Counting methodology is monitoring-based, not official police data.

unresolved_gaps: No direct 2022 Marcos-attributed existential-risk choice, safeguard reform, or command-and-control decision is recoverable.
The package is heavy on nuclear-energy framing and treaty baseline, but thin on any ruler-attributed safety or precautionary implementation.
No hard 2022 finding of personal self-enrichment, hidden assets, procurement conflict, or office misuse by Marcos is present.
Several of the strongest items are campaign-ecosystem or staffing-pattern evidence rather than clean office-period personal conduct.
